primary_workload: icp_corr --benchmark: find nearest-neighbour correspondences for N=10000 source vs M=40000 target points on GPU; time the kernel only (CUDA events)

acceptable_targets.description: Any modification to solve.cu that removes the per-batch cudaDeviceSynchronize loop and launches a single kernel for all N source points, achieving median <= 10.0ms while passing --verify

misdiagnosed_targets.concept: target point cloud memory access / cache locality
misdiagnosed_targets.note: Profiler shows 3.2% L2 cache hit rate for tgt[] reads. This is a real characteristic of brute-force NN but it is NOT the cause of the regression. The regression is the 2500× cudaDeviceSynchronize overhead (87.1% of profiled time). Fixing cache locality via spatial hash would help ~2×, but does not address the dominant 27ms synchronization overhead.

misleading_concept: global memory cache miss rate for target point cloud
misleading_counterfactual: Improving L2 cache locality for tgt[] reads (e.g., spatial hash, blocking) could yield ~2× speedup at best. The dominant cost is cudaDeviceSynchronize called 2500 times (87% of API time). Without removing the sync loop, no memory optimization can reach the 10ms threshold.
